project.title: Oversight Agenda Dashboard
project.description: Seven Democratic oversight investigation areas for the 120th Congress, with leads, next steps, likelihood of moving forward, and impeachment targets.

document.title: Oversight Agenda Dashboard
document.subtitle: Seven investigation areas Democrats are preparing for the Congress that convenes in January 2027, with who leads each, what happens next, and how likely each is to move forward.

items.why: Jeffries is the declared candidate for Speaker. Committee chair slates follow leadership.

items.what: Chairs ratified, staff hired, document requests drafted
items.why: Presumptive chairs are already naming targets and witnesses. Requests go out before formal power arrives.
Subpoena power and committee budgets take effect once the House organizes. Hegseth impeachment articles must be reintroduced.
Garcia has committed to public Epstein hearings. Several investigations are expected to launch at once.

sections.heading: Investigation Areas
sections.legend: Likelihood is an analyst assessment of whether formal investigative activity (hearings, subpoenas, document demands) begins in the first half of 2027. High: a named chair has publicly committed to specific targets or witnesses. Medium: the area appears in party strategy memos and leadership statements but no chair has announced specific actions. Low: the area is in memos only, or the path to action faces a structural block.

cards.title: Pay-to-Play and Public Corruption
cards.lead: House Oversight, Rep. Robert Garcia (presumptive chair)

columns.label: Target areas
items: Government contractors and no-bid contracts
Individuals who received or purchased presidential pardons
Trump family real estate and business dealings
Cryptocurrency frameworks and defense contracts, and whether donations or relationships drove decisions
Corporate donors to the White House ballroom

columns.label: Next steps
items: Garcia has named Stephen Miller, Corey Lewandowski, Kristi Noem and Trump family members as witnesses he will call
Interviews sought with Jared Kushner and other family members on business dealings
Subpoena enforcement planned through lawsuits and civil contempt in court

columns.label: What could slow it
columns.text: DOJ is unlikely to enforce criminal contempt, so non-cooperation drags into litigation. The White House has not committed to cooperating.

columns.label: Basis for the rating
columns.text: The presumptive chair has publicly listed targets and witnesses and described his enforcement plan. This is the most developed area.

cards.title: Tech Industry and AI Policy
cards.lead: Multiple committees; Judiciary (Rep. Jamie Raskin) on antitrust

columns.label: Target areas
items: Executives and informal presidential advisers who shaped federal policy
Companies that committed resources to presidential priorities in exchange for favorable treatment
Administration AI policy, including export controls on advanced semiconductors
Market concentration and circular investments across the AI value chain

columns.label: Next steps
items: Raskin has named corporate mergers and antitrust as a Judiciary focus
No chair has announced AI-specific or export-control hearings yet
Likely first step is document requests to agencies that set AI and chip policy

columns.label: What could slow it
columns.text: Jurisdiction is split across Judiciary, Energy and Commerce, Oversight and Senate committees. Export-control questions touch national security briefings that slow public hearings.

columns.label: Basis for the rating
columns.text: Antitrust has a named chair and a public statement. The AI and export-control pieces appear only in strategy memos so far.

cards.title: DOJ and Regulatory Interference
cards.lead: House Judiciary (Rep. Jamie Raskin); Senate: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (DOJ and antitrust settlements), Sen. Elizabeth Warren (financial regulation)

columns.label: Target areas
items: Politicization of DOJ and FBI, firing of career prosecutors, the $1.8 billion Anti-Weaponization fund
DOJ and antitrust settlements in media and entertainment, and whether they benefited private parties
Bank chartering, supervision decisions and tax settlements driven by political favoritism
Handling of the Epstein investigation, including financial institutions and advisors who may have financed it

columns.label: Next steps
items: Garcia plans public Epstein hearings and may subpoena Attorney General Todd Blanche over withheld pages
Raskin plans Judiciary hearings on DOJ politicization and pay-to-play pardons
Whitehouse and Warren probes on the Senate side have not been formally announced

columns.label: What could slow it
columns.text: Executive privilege and ongoing-investigation claims from DOJ. Senate committee chairs are not yet confirmed.

columns.label: Basis for the rating
columns.text: Two presumptive House chairs have committed to specific hearings and a possible cabinet-level subpoena. The Senate pieces are expected but not announced, so the rating rests on the House side.

cards.title: Public Lands and Freedom250
cards.lead: House Natural Resources, Rep. Jared Huffman (expected chair)

columns.label: Target areas
items: Management of public lands under the administration's environmental policy
Donations tied to Freedom250, the 250th anniversary program
Whether natural resource policy was traded for political or financial support

columns.label: Next steps
items: No post-election statement from Huffman on specific hearings or witnesses
Likely to start with document requests to Interior and the Freedom250 commission
Freedom250 events through July 4, 2027 keep the donor question live

columns.label: What could slow it
columns.text: Not named in any post-election leadership statement. Competes for committee time with legislative priorities and with higher-profile probes.

columns.label: Basis for the rating
columns.text: Appears in strategy memos only. No chair has gone on record since the election.

cards.title: Corporate Accountability and Cost of Living
cards.lead: Rep. Frank Pallone (Energy and Commerce), Sen. Maria Cantwell (Commerce)

columns.label: Target areas
items: Surveillance pricing: using consumer data to charge variable prices
Healthcare and prescription drug costs
Predatory lending
Utilities, fossil fuel operations and large data centers: electricity costs, water use and grid impact

columns.label: Next steps
items: Leadership's first legislative moves are affordability bills: ACA premium subsidies and reversing Medicaid cuts
Oversight hearings on pricing and data centers would run alongside that agenda
No specific hearing dates or witness lists announced

columns.label: What could slow it
columns.text: Leadership wants affordability framed as legislation first. Corporate targets are outside the administration, so hearings draw less media attention than Trump-focused probes.

columns.label: Basis for the rating
columns.text: Named committee leads and a clear leadership priority on cost of living, but no announced hearings. The legislative push may absorb the committee calendar.

cards.title: Impeachment of the President
cards.lead: House Democratic leadership (Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries); House Judiciary (Rep. Jamie Raskin)

columns.label: Target areas
items: Would require explicit evidence from the investigations above, such as direct bribery in defense contracting or pardon-selling

columns.label: Next steps
items: Jeffries: nothing ruled in, nothing ruled out; no caucus member has raised it with him
Raskin: a critical tool, used only if benefits outweigh the cost in time and attention
Any move would follow, not precede, findings from Oversight and Judiciary

columns.label: What could slow it
columns.text: Senate conviction needs 67 votes, which Democrats do not have. Leadership is prioritizing affordability. Some new members say there is no path to removal.

columns.label: Basis for the rating
columns.text: Leadership has deliberately kept it open as leverage, but no one in leadership is advocating it now and the Senate math rules out removal.

cards.title: Impeachment and Removal of Cabinet and Senior Officials
cards.lead: House Judiciary (Rep. Jamie Raskin); House Armed Services (Rep. Adam Smith) on Hegseth; House Oversight (Rep. Robert Garcia) on Blanche and Miller

columns.label: Target areas
items: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth: six articles already filed (Apr 15, 2026) over the Iran war, law of armed conflict, mishandling of military information, obstruction of oversight, and politicizing the armed forces
Attorney General Todd Blanche: handling of Epstein files, including withheld pages; subpoena threatened by Garcia
White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller: named by Jeffries alongside Bondi as someone who has to go; named by Garcia as a witness
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.: impeachment threats from rank-and-file Democrats since December 2025; no post-election leadership statement

columns.label: Next steps
items: Hegseth articles expire with the 119th Congress and must be reintroduced in January; Jeffries has said Democrats will run Hegseth out of town as one of their first actions
Rep. Thomas Massie (R) plans to force a lame-duck vote on his own eight-article Hegseth resolution

Pressure campaigns, not impeachment votes, removed DHS Secretary Kristi Noem (ousted after 50+ Democrats signed articles) and Attorney General Pam Bondi (fired Apr 2, 2026 after articles over Epstein documents); expect the same pattern first

columns.label: What could slow it
columns.text: Only two cabinet officials have ever been impeached (Belknap 1876, Mayorkas 2024) and neither was convicted. Senate conviction still needs 67 votes. Raskin, Schiff and Crow are described as cautious on impeachment.

columns.label: Basis for the rating
columns.text: Articles against Hegseth exist with cosponsors, the Speaker-designate has committed publicly to removing him, and the likely Armed Services chair is inclined to back proceedings. The rating covers formal action beginning, not conviction.

tiles.label: House: to impeach
tiles.note: Simple majority. Democrats are projected to hold it. Applies to the President and to any civil officer.

tiles.label: Senate: to convict
tiles.note: Two-thirds. A 7-seat gain leaves Democrats well short without Republican votes.

tiles.label: Cabinet precedent
tiles.note: Cabinet officials ever impeached: Belknap (1876) and Mayorkas (2024). Neither was convicted.

sections.legend: Likelihood here means formal House action (reintroduced articles, Judiciary hearings, or a floor vote) in the first half of 2027, not Senate conviction. The Noem and Bondi rows show the pattern so far: pressure campaigns backed by filed articles led to removal before any impeachment vote.
